title: Tiered batching defaults — rollout checklist (Hosted/Dedicated/Private)
linked_artifacts: GitHub: redwood/pr_18515 (canary rollout tooling + auto rollback hooks)
GitHub: redwood/pr_18449 (queue delay + batch formation metrics)
GitHub: redwood/pr_18463 (streaming cadence regression fix in fast tier)
content:
Doc purpose
- This is the working checklist for rolling out workload-aware batching defaults (fast / standard / cost-efficient) behind a feature flag.
- It’s written for the runtime + SRE on-call path: what to check, where to look, who decides, and what “stop” looks like.

Scope notes (read me)
- Applies to: Hosted API first; Dedicated next; Private (VPC/on-prem) last via runtime-1.21 + config migration.
- Non-goal: we are not doing per-customer bespoke tuning in this rollout. Only tiered defaults + guardrails.
- Precedence: explicit batching knobs override tier defaults. (If we see regressions, first question is always “was there an explicit override?”)

Owners / decision makers
- Rollout on-call / go-no-go: Rafael Mendes (SRE), backup Sean Gallagher
- Runtime parameter changes: Sofia Ivanova
- Feature flag mechanics / targeting: Benji Okafor
- Dashboards + alert thresholds: Allison Grant
- Product comms + customer opt-in/out language: Aditya Rao
- Release train / branch cut: Connor O'Brien
- Quality gate sign-off: Jonas Weber (Applied ML)

Slack channels / escalation
- Primary: #eng-runtime, #eng-sre, #releases-runtime
- Incident path: #incidents (page SRE on-call; loop in Sofia + Benji)
- Customer-facing coordination: #support, #customer-success (via Miguel Santos)

Feature flag(s) (current as of runtime-1.21)
- Flag name(s):
  - batching_tier_defaults_enabled (global enable)
  - batching_tier_defaults_targeting (model/region/customer targeting rules)
  - batching_tier_autorollback_enabled (hooked to SRE signals)
- Targeting dimensions supported:
  - model family / variant
  - region
  - route type (chat/completions/embeddings; streaming vs non-streaming)
  - customer tier (internal, beta cohort, general)

Pre-rollout prerequisites (must be green before ANY ramp)
[ ] 1) Runtime build + schema landed
    - Runtime version tagged for rollout (runtime-1.21.x).
    - Config schema includes batching_tier: fast | standard | cost_efficient.
    - “Explain effective config” endpoint working so Console + support can debug (see GitHub redwood/pr_18470).

[ ] 2) Metrics present in prod and validated (labels correct)
    Required minimum metrics for tier monitoring:
    - Request latency: p50/p95/p99 by (tier, model, region, route, streaming)
    - Queue delay: histogram p50/p95/p99 by (tier, model, region)
    - Batch formation: batch_size histogram; batches_per_min; mean batch fill
    - GPU util: SM util %, memory util %, KV cache pressure
    - Errors: 5xx rate, timeout rate, cancellation rate, load-shed counters + reason code
    - Streaming cadence: time-to-first-token (TTFT) and tokens/sec distribution (where available)
    Validation steps:
    - Compare counts to pre-flag baseline; ensure no label cardinality blowups.
    - Confirm dashboards render for at least 2 models in 2 regions.

[ ] 3) Perf canary is green on all required lanes
    - perf-canary tier suite passing (fast/standard/cost-efficient) for top models and at least 2 GPU SKUs.
    - No unexplained p95 regressions vs baseline. (If borderline, annotate with benchmark-lab output + rationale.)

[ ] 4) Quality gate complete for this release candidate
    - Prompt-set evals run with tiered defaults enabled for the launch cohort models.
    - Deltas within guardrails (see quality guardrails doc). If any failures: block rollout until triaged.

[ ] 5) Rollback automation is configured AND tested
    - Auto-rollback hooks wired to the chosen signals (see “Abort conditions”).
    - Run a dry-run in staging: trigger threshold, confirm flag reverts, confirm alert fires.

[ ] 6) Comms artifacts ready
    - Internal: #eng-runtime + #eng-sre announcement draft ready with exact schedule.
    - External: beta opt-in/out instructions ready (support macros + docs link).
    - Release notes stub ready for runtime-1.21 (Connor owns).

Dashboards to watch (bookmarks for rollout)
- Tiered latency overview: p50/p95/p99 by tier + model + region
- Queue delay heatmap: queue_delay_ms p95 and tail over time
- Batch formation distributions: batch size histogram + batch wait time
- GPU health: util %, memory %, OOM/restart counters, KV cache pressure
- Error & overload: timeout/cancel, 5xx, load-shed rate + reason codes
- Streaming: TTFT p95 and token cadence (tokens/sec) vs baseline
- “Effective config sampling”: top effective batching parameters by tier (to catch unexpected overrides)

Definitions: what success looks like (rollout acceptance)
- Standard tier should be safe default: no material p95 regression vs pre-tier baseline for most workloads; improves throughput/$ in steady state.
- Fast tier must protect streaming: stable TTFT and cadence; queue delay stays small.
- Cost-efficient tier can trade latency for cost, but must not increase timeout/error rates; must remain stable under overload protection.

Abort conditions (STOP / rollback triggers)
Hard stops (immediate rollback + incident-style thread)
- [ ] Timeout rate increases by >0.20% absolute (tiered traffic) for 10+ minutes in any region for launch models.
- [ ] 5xx increases by >0.10% absolute for 10+ minutes (excluding known dependent incidents).
- [ ] Any OOM/restart rate increase correlated with tier enablement (KV cache pressure spike + pod restarts).
- [ ] Streaming cadence regression: TTFT p95 +20% vs baseline for 15+ minutes on fast tier routes.
- [ ] Queue delay p99 exceeds tier budget (see SLO tier doc) for 15+ minutes, AND correlates with increased cancellations/timeouts.

Soft stops (pause ramp; keep current percentage; triage within same day)
- [ ] p95 latency increases beyond tier target on a single model/region lane, without errors.
- [ ] GPU util is unexpectedly low (indicates misconfiguration) or too high (sustained >95% with rising queue delay).
- [ ] Batch size distribution shifts abruptly (e.g., average batch size doubles) outside expected parameter changes.

Notes on interpreting signals
- Queue delay alone can be noisy; use it with cancellations/timeouts and p95/p99 latency. Allison to confirm alert thresholds aren’t too aggressive (see #eng-sre thread 1740752220).
- Streaming regressions often show first in TTFT, then in customer-reported “choppy stream”. Treat early signals seriously.

Rollout stages (recommended sequence)
Stage 0 — Staging verification (1–2 days)
[ ] Enable batching_tier_defaults_enabled in staging at 100% for target models.
[ ] Run targeted load (streaming + non-streaming + long-context) and validate dashboards.
[ ] Confirm “effective config” endpoint returns expected parameters per tier.
[ ] Confirm auto-rollback wiring works (staging test).

Stage 1 — Internal dogfood (prod, internal traffic only)
Target: 1–5% of internal org traffic, limited models/regions.
[ ] Enable for internal service accounts only (Benji).
[ ] Watch dashboards for 2 hours minimum during business hours.
[ ] Collect runtime engineer feedback in #eng-runtime (esp. streaming routes).
Go/no-go:
- Go if no hard-stop signals and p95 stable.
- Pause if any soft-stop signals; diagnose before expanding.

Stage 2 — Canary (prod, narrow model/region)
Target: 1% of external traffic for 1–2 models in 1–2 regions.
[ ] Choose canary lane (SRE + Product): typically a high-volume model with stable baseline.
[ ] Enable standard tier default only (do NOT auto-apply cost-efficient by default at this stage).
[ ] Hold for 24 hours (cover peak + off-peak).
[ ] Verify error budgets unaffected.

Stage 3 — Beta cohort (opt-in customers)
Target: 5–15 accounts with known workloads and explicit success criteria.
[ ] Confirm cohort list + owners (Aditya + Miguel).
[ ] Send opt-in instructions + how to validate (dashboards/headers).
[ ] Schedule 30-min check-in per account within first week.
[ ] Capture issues as tickets (Support + Linear) with: model, region, route, streaming, tier, and explicit overrides.
Special attention:
- Cost-efficient tier: require overload protection alignment to be enabled (see redwood/pr_18488). If not, block cost-efficient opt-in.

Stage 4 — Gradual ramp (standard tier as default for selected routes)
Target: 10% → 25% → 50% → 100% (per lane), with holds.
Recommended hold times:
- 10% for 6 hours
- 25% for 12 hours
- 50% for 24 hours
- 100% after at least one full day at 50% with no issues
Checklist per step:
[ ] Pre-step snapshot: baseline p95/p99, timeouts, queue delay p95/p99.
[ ] Apply new percentage.
[ ] Watch first 30 minutes closely (tail spikes show quickly).
[ ] If stable, continue hold; if soft-stop, pause; if hard-stop, rollback.

Stage 5 — Expand model/region coverage
[ ] Expand to additional regions one at a time (avoid multi-region simultaneous ramps).
[ ] Expand to additional model families, prioritizing those with benchmark coverage.
[ ] For long-context-heavy models: confirm model/GPU overrides are set in model registry before enabling (avoid KV cache pressure surprises).

Stage 6 — Dedicated + Private
Dedicated:
[ ] Confirm dedicated customers’ autoscaling policies and headroom (queue delay behavior differs with fixed capacity).
[ ] Roll out via account-level enablement first.
Private:
[ ] Ensure helm chart values + installer migrations validated (config is backwards compatible).
[ ] Provide “what changed” notes and rollback steps to SE/Support.

Rollback procedure (manual)
- Immediate action: set batching_tier_defaults_enabled = false for the impacted lane.
- If issue persists after rollback: check if customers have explicit overrides; isolate by route/model.
- Capture artifacts:
  - dashboard screenshots (before/after)
  - config explain output (effective parameters)
  - a few trace IDs (tail latency samples)
- Post in #incidents with:
  - start time
  - scope (model/region/routes)
  - customer impact estimate
  - rollback confirmation

Comms checklist
Internal (every ramp change)
[ ] Post in #eng-runtime and #eng-sre: what changed, where, percent, and what dashboards we’re watching.
[ ] Confirm who is watching for first 30 minutes (name a person, not “team”).

External (beta / customer impacts)
[ ] If a beta customer is affected: notify Support + CSM owner with summary and next steps.
[ ] If widespread impact (timeouts/5xx): follow incident comms policy; coordinate with on-call and leadership.

Post-rollout wrap-up (after stable 100% on initial lanes)
[ ] Write brief summary: results vs goals ($/token estimate, latency changes, error rates) and link benchmark-lab output.
[ ] Capture parameter tuning backlog by model/GPU SKU (Linear follow-ups).
[ ] Confirm docs reflect reality (tier names, overrides, how to view effective config).

Open questions / TODO (keep current)
- Alert thresholds: queue delay p99 is noisy for some lanes; Allison to tune alerts to reduce false positives without missing true overload.
- Streaming cadence measurement coverage: not all routes emit tokens/sec consistently; Julian to confirm instrumentation for the launch models.
- “Cost-efficient default” policy: Product leaning towards opt-in only for GA; revisit after beta data.

Change log
- 2025-03-18 (Rafael): added hard-stop for TTFT regression (+20% p95) after fast-tier streaming issue; clarified hold times per ramp step.
- 2025-03-10 (Allison): updated dashboard list to include load-shed reason codes + KV cache pressure.
- 2025-02-20 (Rafael): initial draft from PM-412 launch plan + SRE tier SLO doc.
